summary: Master Human Rights-Based Approaches to Social Protection. Learn to design inclusive, accountable safety nets aligned with ILO and UN standards. Enroll today.
lede: Human Rights-Based Approaches to Social Protection helps social protection officers, programme managers, and human rights advisers design interventions that promote participation, accessibility, non-discrimination, and effective remedies. The course draws on the ICESCR, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, the ILO Social Protection Floors Recommendation, 2012 (No. 202), and principles promoted by OHCHR. You will apply the PANEL principles and rights-based programming tools to assess eligibility and delivery processes, map rights-holders and duty-bearers, review accessibility, and strengthen grievance mechanisms. Practical exercises address digital registries, automated decision controls, and AI-assisted risk screening at an operational awareness level, leading to an implementation plan, assessment templates, and a reporting structure for monitoring rights-based outcomes.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape, administer, monitor, or scrutinize social protection policies and delivery systems. It suits intermediate-level practitioners who can relate policy choices to programme operations and need a structured human rights-based social protection method.
modules: Human Rights and Social Protection Foundations
prerequisites: You should have practical experience in social protection policy, programme delivery, human rights programming, social services, monitoring and evaluation, or public-sector planning. Familiarity with benefit schemes, programme indicators, and institutional reporting is useful. No coding or programming is required. Advanced digital topics are taught at conceptual awareness and operational application levels, with hands-on spreadsheet and dashboard exercises using provided sample data.
